Born: August 4, 1961, 7:24 PM local time, Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Barack Obama's chart on Astrolas to follow the wheel while you read.

One contact sets the tone for the whole chart. Y Jupiter and U Saturn sit conjunct in the 12th house, the part of the chart the Astrolas library ties to work done out of public view before any result shows. Around that core sit two clusters: the Sun and Mercury together in Leo in the 6th house of daily work, and Mars, Uranus and Pluto all gathered in the 7th house of partnership. Read together, they describe a rise built in stages, mostly out of sight, before the public parts caught up.

muc.ten: Jupiter conjunct Saturn in the 12th house
doan: Jupiter sits at 0°52' Aquarius, retrograde, and Saturn at 25°20' Capricorn, retrograde, both in the 12th house, conjunct at an orb of 5°32'.

The library reads this conjunction as Jupiter's optimism meeting Saturn's practicality: idealism runs into real obstacles, and frustration is part of the process, but the capacity for hard work and persistence is the greatest asset here. Success tends to arrive slowly, in both career and finances, but it lasts once it comes. Saturn in Capricorn on its own is, in the library's words, Saturn at its fullest strength: ambitious, disciplined and self-reliant from a young age, climbing step by step rather than in one leap. In the 12th house, that climb happens quietly, with recognition arriving late and real growth coming through facing self-doubt rather than blaming circumstances. Jupiter in Aquarius adds a pull toward social justice, group ideals and the kind of luck that runs through alliances and causes rather than individual effort; in the 12th house, the library notes a tendency to serve from behind the scenes rather than from the spotlight.

Obama's path from a community organizer in Chicago, to an Illinois state senator in 1997, to the United States Senate in 2005, to the presidency in 2009, took more than a decade of exactly the kind of unglamorous, incremental work this placement describes, much of it well outside national attention until late in the sequence.

muc.ten: Sun and Mercury in Leo, house 6
doan: The Sun sits at 12°33' g Leo , and Mercury at 2°20' Leo, both in the 6th house, the library's house of work and daily service.

The library's Leo Sun is confident and magnetic, drawn to leadership and public presence, happiest when affirming its own worth while lifting others. Sun in the 6th house ties that identity directly to work itself: a strong self-image built through being useful, attentive to detail, and recognized for a job done well, with a caution against working without rest. Mercury in Leo adds a communicator's confidence, a dramatic and persuasive style suited to public speaking, while Mercury in the 6th wants work that keeps the mind engaged and rewards precision.

Obama worked for years as a civil rights attorney and law lecturer before and alongside his political career, and his rise owed a great deal to his ability as a speaker, most visibly in the 2004 speech to the Democratic National Convention that first brought him wide national notice.

muc.ten: Mars, Uranus and Pluto in the 7th house
doan: Mars sits at 22°35' h Virgo and Pluto at 6°59' Virgo, both in the 7th house, with Uranus at 25°16' Leo also in the 7th, the library's house of partnership.

The library's Mars in Virgo is precise and analytical, well suited to law, politics or investigation, where staying objective rather than emotional is an advantage. In the 7th house, that same energy shows up as a strong, sometimes competitive drive inside close relationships, with a caution to listen and compromise rather than push for the lead. Uranus in Leo is generational for his entire cohort; personally, through the 7th house, the library reads it as an attraction to distinctive, independent partners and a bond built on friendship as much as romance. Pluto in Virgo is also generational, tied to a cohort reshaping labor and public service; through the 7th house, it becomes personal as a pull toward partnerships that transform both people, with jealousy and control named as the things to watch.

Obama married his wife, Michelle, in 1992, and their partnership has been a constant, public feature of his career ever since, matching the competitive, relationship-tested drive the library reads into this Mars.
The Moon sits at 3°21' d Gemini , in the 4th house.

The library's Gemini Moon processes feeling through the mind, changeable, talkative, quick to turn an emotion into words on the page rather than sit inside it. Moon in the 4th house ties that need for expression to family and roots, with the library naming an interest some people with this placement develop in tracing their own ancestry. Obama spent part of his childhood in Hawaii and Indonesia, the son of a father from Kenya and a mother from Kansas, and his first book, Dreams from My Father, published in 1995, is built directly around that search for his father and his own origins.
Venus sits at 1°47' f Cancer , in the 5th house.

The library's Cancer Venus is romantic and loyal, seeking emotional and material security before opening up fully, and devoted once committed. Venus in the 5th house adds warmth expressed through quiet, thoughtful gestures rather than display, along with real pleasure taken in children. He and Michelle Obama have two daughters, Malia, born in 1998, and Sasha, born in 2001.
Neptune sits at 8°36' Scorpio, in the 9th house, the library's house of higher learning, publishing and foreign horizons.

Neptune in Scorpio is generational, tied by the library to a cohort drawn to uncovering hidden truths; in the 9th house, it becomes personal as strong intuition paired with success through creative or instinctive insight, often alongside a pull toward philosophy or belief systems formed across cultures. Obama earned his law degree from Harvard in 1991, where he served as president of the Harvard Law Review, and published a second book, The Audacity of Hope, in 2006, before a post-presidency memoir, A Promised Land, in 2020.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart does not explain how any particular vote or speech landed. What it shows is a shape: a Jupiter-Saturn conjunction built for slow, step-by-step advance, working quietly in the 12th house, with a confident Leo voice in the 6th house of daily work and a partnership-heavy 7th house running alongside it. The Ascendant sits at 18°03' Aquarius, with the Midheaven at 28°53' Scorpio; the Astrolas library has no entries yet for either placement on its own, so this piece does not build a reading on them.
